tools.name: datailo_start_here
tools.description: Orientation for a new connection: the cross-service jobs you can hand over (listed first), which services are enabled, which are available, and what to do next. Call this first.

tools.name: datailo_connect
tools.description: Sign in, inside the chat (needed to enable services and call their tools). Send the user's email and the language you are speaking with them (e.g. 'lt', 'en', 'de'). tools.description: Finish signing in. Call it RIGHT AFTER datailo_connect with the request_id and no code: it waits up to 45 s for the user to click Confirm in the email and returns as soon as they do (call again if it returns waiting — do not ask the user to report the click). If the user reads you the six-digit code

tools.name: datailo_account
tools.description: The connected account's email, service links, and plan states. action='keys' lists your dat_ keys (prefix, origin, created, last used — never the key); action='revoke_key' with key_prefix revokes one.

tools.name: datailo_catalog
tools.description: Compact rows for every federated service: name, job, datasets, tool and workflow counts, tiers, whether it is enabled on this account. Rendered from each service's live product card, never hand-written; a service without a card yet shows card: "unavailable".

tools.name: datailo_describe
tools.description: The full product card for one service: tagline, datasets, workflows, tiers, docs.

tools.name: datailo_enable
tools.description: Enable a federated service on your Datailo account. For services with an account model the hub links (or creates) your account there by your email and keeps an encrypted key; keyless services are enabled as a trial. Then datailo_tools and datailo_invoke reach it through this one connection.

tools.name: datailo_disable
tools.description: Disable a service: revokes the hub's key for it. Your account and data there remain yours.

tools.name: datailo_plan
tools.description: See a service's plans or record that you want to enroll, change or discontinue one (action: status | enroll | change | discontinue). Payments are not enabled yet: a choice is recorded as an intent, nothing is charged and no checkout link is returned.

tools.name: datailo_tools
tools.description: Search the tools of your enabled services (read live from each service). q takes words or a whole sentence: tools are ranked by the words they match, name and title first. service narrows to one service; include_available also previews services you could enable; limit caps the list (default 50).

tools.name: datailo_tool_schema
tools.description: The full input schema for one tool of an enabled service, and how to call it.

tools.name: datailo_invoke
tools.description: Call one tool of an enabled service through the hub: service, tool name and its arguments (see datailo_tool_schema). Returns the service's own result.

tools.name: datailo_workflows
tools.description: Cross-service jobs first (service 'datailo', kind 'job': whole work products that chain several services), then each service's ready-made playbooks, marked enabled or not. Open one with datailo_workflow.

tools.name: datailo_workflow
tools.description: One playbook's steps from the service itself, each annotated with the exact datailo_invoke call to run it through this connection. service='datailo' with a job name returns the whole job: services to enable, stages with their playbooks, checkpoints and the work-product template.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "datailo_connect" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Anomalously long tool description
findings.detail: Description of "submit_feedback" is 1414 chars, far longer than this server's median (254). Overlong descriptions are a common place to bury instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: notifications · Private data: datailo_plan · Public sink: datailo_connect, datailo_connect_verify, datailo_account, datailo_enable, submit_feedback, notifications · Destructive: datailo_workflow, notifications.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: notifications · Private data: datailo_plan · Public sink: datailo_connect, datailo_connect_verify, datailo_account, datailo_enable, submit_feedback, notifications · Destructive: datailo_workflow, notifications

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
